name: Juan Gualberto Gomez International Airport
before:
Varadero's airport, and second busiest in Cuba after Havana. It is 5 km from the village of Carbonera and actually closer to Matanzas than to Varadero itself, so build a real transfer into any resort booking.

The European picture has changed and it is worth knowing before quoting. TUI ended all its Varadero flying in 2024, having served the airport from Amsterdam and Brussels, after a sharp fall in passenger numbers to Cuba, and Condor announced in 2025 that it would drop its Frankfurt route. Check what is actually operating rather than relying on an older programme.

The terminal is straightforward. There are four jet bridges serving stands 2 to 5, with air stairs for the remaining stand. Departures is upstairs with cafeterias and a large lounge, and there is a smaller air conditioned VIP lounge below. Shops sell rum, cigars, books and carvings both before and after customs.

The airport was built in 1989 and opened by Fidel Castro, replacing the older Varadero airport at Santa Marta, now Kawama. It is named after Juan Gualberto Gómez, the journalist and independence campaigner.
after:
Varadero's airport, named after Juan Gualberto Gómez. It lies near Carbonera and is actually closer to Matanzas than to Varadero itself, so build a real transfer into any resort booking.

In 2026 Cuba's international airports, this one included, have run short of jet fuel. All the Canadian airlines have suspended their Cuba flights. TUI had already stopped flying here in 2024 after demand for Cuba fell sharply, ending its flights from Amsterdam and Belgium and its Manchester service, then the UK's only direct route to Cuba. Condor followed in 2025. Check what is actually operating rather than relying on an older programme.

claims.claim: in 2026 Cuba's international airports, Varadero's included, have run short of jet fuel
claims.inAfter: In 2026 Cuba's international airports, this one included, have run short of jet fuel
claims.note: Replaces the old framing 'The European picture has changed' (cut below): the old paragraph's point was which airlines have stopped flying here, and in 2026 the change is no longer European. Like for like: airlines that have stopped flying, and why. The FCDO says Cuba's authorities have announced that all its international airports are without aviation fuel; CiberCuba, in its July 2026 report on the airport, names Varadero among the airports that have been unable to guarantee Jet A-1 since at least February 2026. 'Run short' is the common ground between 'without' and 'cannot guarantee'. The FCDO's headline advice itself replaces nothing and is held back (below).

claims.claim: Condor stopped flying here in 2025
claims.note: Was 'Condor announced in 2025 that it would drop its Frankfurt route'. aeroTELEGRAPH (undated on the saved page, but it quotes a 5 December 2024 update and speaks of 'next summer') has a Condor spokeswoman confirming no Cuba flights for summer 2025 and the last Varadero flight on 29 April 2025, so the announcement came in late 2024 and the ending in 2025. Condor's own Caribbean page, read today, lists its destinations for summer 2026, winter 2026/27 and summer 2027 with no Cuban airport, so it has not come back. 'Frankfurt' is dropped: for Varadero it rests on Wikipedia alone.

Its source, Fidel Castro's speech of 25 September 1989 on the Cuban government portal (cuba.cu), failed to connect; EcuRed timed out; the University of Texas copy of Castro's speeches (LANIC) answered 503. Each was tried once. OurAirports does list Kawama Airport at Santa Marta, with Varadero as a keyword and no scheduled service, which fits, but says nothing of 1989, Castro or a replacement. Worth restoring when a Cuban source can be read.

claims.claim: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba
claims.why: Held back, and recommended for Andy as the most important line for this airport: a warning that replaces nothing in the old text, so under the like-for-like rule it stays out. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba (updated 16 July 2026, still current at 24 September 2026): the national grid collapsed for the third time in a week on 14 July, the government said on 13 May that diesel and fuel oil reserves were exhausted, there have been protests, and from 6 June international cards such as Visa and Mastercard are not accepted, so visitors need cash for their whole stay. The Government of Canada also says to avoid non-essential travel (updated 22 September 2026), warning that fuel shortages disrupt ground transport and taxis, which bears on the transfer advice. A suggested attributed sentence: 'The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba.'

sources.org: UK FCDO (Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office)
quote: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba.
On 14 July, the Cuban National Electric grid collapsed for the third time in a week.
On 13 May, the Cuban government announced that the country had exhausted its reserves of diesel and fuel oil.
On 3 June the Cuban Central Bank announced that international cards such as Visa and Mastercard will no longer be accepted in Cuba, with effect from 6 June.
Avoid non-essential travel to Cuba due to worsening shortages of fuel, electricity, and basic necessities including food, water, and medicine.
Public transportation services, including taxis, are often disrupted, leaving tourists with few options to travel.

claims.claim: Varadero's flights in mid-2026: one airline in June, practically at a standstill in July
claims.why: Held back: one organisation only. CiberCuba reported on 4 June 2026, from the airport company's (ECASA's) own published data, that American Airlines from Miami, four days a week, was the only airline linking Varadero with the outside world that month, after the Canadian and Russian airlines left; on 8 July 2026 it reported the airport 'practically paralysed', leasing out four fuel tanks under a tender whose contract is 'subject to the restart of airport operations'. No second organisation could be read to confirm the Varadero detail (the Cuban-hosted sites tried did not connect; the airport company's own Telegram channels, which CiberCuba cites, were not tried). If it can be confirmed, it is the line that says how busy the airport is now.

quote: Varadero, el principal destino turístico de playa del país, solo cuenta con vuelos de American Airlines desde Miami, operados los lunes, jueves, viernes y domingos.
Es la única aerolínea que conecta ese destino con el exterior en junio
supeditado al reinicio de las operaciones aeroportuarias
Miércoles, 8 Julio, 2026
